subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should OpenClaw allow ordinary same-session Discord and bound-thread messages to bypass active reply-operation/channel serialization into queue policy, and if so which owner boundary should enforce the safety checks?
rationale: The behavior is user-visible and documented, but the remaining implementation changes message ordering and session ownership semantics across channel ingress and reply admission.

options.title: Coordinate the admission-layer fix
options.body: Use or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 with a maintained branch that preserves current runtime steering and fallback semantics.

options.title: Narrow to Discord ACP only
options.body: Limit the fix to Discord bound ACP/sub-agent threads first, leaving other channel ingress designs to the broader canonical issue.

options.title: Defer ordinary-message steering
options.body: Keep only explicit control commands and terminal/TUI steering for now, documenting ordinary chat messages as followups until a broader ingress design is approved.

recommendation.title: Coordinate the admission-layer fix
recommendation.body: Use or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89238 with a maintained branch that preserves current runtime steering and fallback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership is concentrated in the reply admission, active-run registry, and channel queue surfaces that need the decision.
